title: Đề luyện Đọc VSTEP — Review HVNH HN 18/8/2026 (3/4 passage)

passages.p1:
# Two Ways to Get Married in Japan

In Japan today, couples who decide to marry usually choose between two very different kinds of ceremony. The first is the traditional Shinto wedding, which has been held for hundreds of years. The second is the Western-style wedding, which became popular only in recent decades. Although the two look quite different, both remain common, and some couples even hold both.

A Shinto wedding takes place at a shrine and is led by a priest. The bride wears a white kimono and a special headpiece, while the groom wears a dark formal kimono. During the ceremony, the couple sip rice wine, called sake, three times from three cups, a ritual that is believed to join the two families together. Only close relatives usually attend this part, so the atmosphere is quiet and serious rather than crowded. Prayers are offered to the gods for a long and healthy marriage.

The Western-style wedding, by contrast, is held in a chapel or a hotel hall. The bride wears a long white dress and the groom wears a suit, much as couples do in Europe or America. A person dressed as a minister often guides the ceremony, and the couple exchange rings in front of their guests. Many young people prefer this style because they have seen it in films and think it looks romantic. It is also easier to invite a large number of friends.

Interestingly, the choice of ceremony does not always match a couple's religion. Most Japanese people are not Christian, yet the white-dress chapel wedding is chosen by more than half of all couples. For many of them, the Western style is simply a fashion, not a statement of faith. Older family members, however, may still prefer the Shinto ceremony because it feels closer to Japanese tradition.

The cost of the two styles can also be very different. A grand hotel wedding with hundreds of guests can be extremely expensive, while a small shrine ceremony is usually cheaper. To save money, some couples now hold only a simple ceremony and spend the rest on their honeymoon or their new home.

Whichever style they choose, most Japanese weddings share one thing: after the ceremony there is a large party, called a reception, where guests eat, give speeches and offer gifts of money in special envelopes. In the end, the type of ceremony matters less than the meaning behind it — two people, and often two families, promising to share their future.
passages.p2:
# When Smoke Meets Fog

The word "smog" was invented more than a hundred years ago by joining two ordinary words: "smoke" and "fog". It describes the dirty, yellow-grey haze that hangs over a city when polluted air cannot escape. Today smog is one of the most visible signs of air pollution, and several of the world's largest cities struggle with it for months at a time.

The most famous case in history happened in London in 1952. For five days, cold weather trapped smoke from coal fires close to the ground, mixing it with thick winter fog. The air became so poisonous that thousands of people died from breathing problems, and drivers could barely see the road in front of them. This disaster, later called the Great Smog, finally forced the government to pass laws limiting the burning of coal.

Modern smog, however, is often different from the coal smoke of the past. In warm, sunny cities such as Los Angeles, much of the haze appears when sunlight reacts with gases from car exhausts. This type is known as photochemical smog, and it tends to be worst on hot, still afternoons when there is no wind to carry the pollution away. Cities surrounded by mountains suffer the most, because the hills act like walls that keep the dirty air trapped in a bowl.

The effects of smog reach far beyond poor visibility. Tiny particles in the haze can travel deep into the lungs and even pass into the blood, raising the risk of heart and breathing diseases. Children, elderly people and those who already suffer from asthma are especially at risk. On the worst days, schools may close and outdoor sport is cancelled, while hospitals report a sharp rise in patients.

Governments have tried many solutions with mixed results. Some cities limit how often private cars may be driven, allowing them out only on certain days according to their number plates. Others invest heavily in electric buses and cleaner factories, or move heavy industry away from where people live. A few have planted wide "green belts" of trees in the hope that the leaves will trap some of the dust.

None of these measures works overnight, and progress is often slow and uneven. Yet the example of London offers some hope. The city that once suffered the deadliest smog in history now enjoys far cleaner air than it did seventy years ago, proving that determined action, though difficult, can gradually clear even the darkest skies.
passages.p3:
# What's on Our Plates This Year

Every year, food experts try to guess which dishes, ingredients and habits will become popular. These predictions are known as "food trends", and they say a great deal about how our tastes — and our worries — are changing. This year, several clear trends have appeared on menus and in supermarkets around the world.

The biggest trend is the rise of plant-based food. More and more people are choosing meals made from vegetables, beans and grains instead of meat. Some do this to protect their health, others because raising animals uses a great deal of land and water. Food companies have noticed, and shops now sell burgers, sausages and even "chicken" made entirely from plants. Ten years ago these products tasted strange to many people; today some are so close to real meat that customers cannot tell the difference.

A second trend is a growing interest in food from other cultures, especially the everyday street food of Asia, Africa and Latin America. Instead of expensive restaurant meals, diners want the bold, spicy flavours that ordinary families cook at home. Dishes that were once hard to find outside their home countries now appear at food markets in almost every big city. For many young people, trying these flavours is a cheap and exciting way to travel without leaving town.

Waste is another word on everyone's lips. Restaurants and shoppers are becoming ashamed of throwing food away, and clever cooks now use parts that were once dropped in the bin, such as vegetable skins and stale bread. Some restaurants proudly serve "root-to-leaf" dishes that use the whole plant, while apps help customers buy unsold food cheaply at the end of the day. Saving money and protecting the planet, it turns out, can go hand in hand.

Technology is quietly shaping what we eat as well. Many people now order meals through their phones, follow cooking videos online, and even let websites suggest recipes based on whatever is left in their fridge. Critics warn that staring at food on a screen is no substitute for cooking and eating together, but few can deny how convenient these tools have become.

Not every trend will last. Some clever-sounding ideas disappear within months, while a few quietly become a normal part of daily life. What seems certain is that food will keep changing, driven by our wish to eat well, spend less and take better care of the world we share.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. The special clothes worn at Japanese weddings.
B. The long history of shrines built across Japan.
C. Two different wedding styles that Japanese couples use.
D. The party and money gifts given after the wedding.
questions.explanation: Đáp án C. Câu mở đầu nêu người Nhật thường chọn giữa hai kiểu lễ cưới rất khác nhau; cả bài triển khai so sánh hai kiểu. A/B/D chỉ là chi tiết nhỏ, không phải chủ đề chung.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

Where is a Shinto wedding held?
options: A. At a shrine, guided by a priest.
B. In a hotel hall, led by someone dressed as a minister.
C. Inside a chapel, with the couple exchanging rings.
D. In a church, much as couples do in Europe.
questions.explanation: Đáp án A. Bài nói lễ Thần đạo diễn ra tại đền thờ, do thầy tế chủ trì. Nhà nguyện/sảnh khách sạn (B, D) là của lễ phương Tây; C không được nhắc.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

What do the couple do three times during a Shinto ceremony?
options: A. They tie a cord to join the two families together.
B. They drink a little rice wine from small cups.
C. They light three candles for their parents.
D. They bow three times to all the guests.
questions.explanation: Đáp án B. Nghi thức là nhấp rượu gạo (sake) ba lần từ ba chén. Trao nhẫn (A) thuộc lễ phương Tây; C, D không được nhắc trong lễ Thần đạo.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

Why is the atmosphere of a Shinto wedding described as quiet?
options: A. Speaking is forbidden inside every shrine.
B. The guests must pray for the whole day.
C. The shrine building itself is very small and plain.
D. Usually only close family members are present.
questions.explanation: Đáp án D. Bài giải thích không khí yên tĩnh vì thường chỉ người thân gần có mặt. A/B/C không được nêu là lý do.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

According to the passage, why do many young people like the Western style?
options: A. The bride can wear a beautiful long white dress.
B. It lets them marry just like people in Europe.
C. It looks romantic, like the weddings shown in movies.
D. The couple can exchange rings before all their guests.
questions.explanation: Đáp án C. Người trẻ thích vì đã xem trong phim và thấy lãng mạn. Bài không nói nó do tôn giáo yêu cầu (A), rẻ hơn (B) hay nhanh (D).

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

What does the passage suggest about the white-dress chapel wedding?
options: A. It is chosen only by couples who are Christian.
B. It is popular even among couples of no particular faith.
C. It is now chosen by nearly every couple in Japan.
D. It is always cheaper than a shrine ceremony.
questions.explanation: Đáp án B. Dù đa số người Nhật không theo Cơ Đốc giáo, hơn nửa số cặp vẫn chọn lễ nhà nguyện → phổ biến cả với người ngoài đạo. A trái với ý bài; C, D không có căn cứ.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

What is said about the cost of the two styles?
options: A. A shrine ceremony is normally the more affordable choice.
B. The size of the guest list barely affects the total cost.
C. A large hotel wedding is the cheaper option.
D. Prices for both styles have fallen in recent years.
questions.explanation: Đáp án A. Lễ nhỏ ở đền thờ thường rẻ hơn, còn tiệc khách sạn lớn rất tốn kém → lễ đền thờ là lựa chọn tiết kiệm hơn. B, C, D đều trái với bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

Why do some couples now hold only a simple ceremony?
options: A. So that they can spend far more on the reception party.
B. Because older relatives now insist on Japanese tradition.
C. So they can keep money for other important things.
D. Because a shrine allows only a few close relatives to attend.
questions.explanation: Đáp án C. Họ làm lễ đơn giản để tiết kiệm và dành tiền cho tuần trăng mật hoặc nhà mới. A trái ý (đơn giản không phải để mời thêm khách); B, D không được nêu.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

What usually happens after the ceremony?
options: A. The couple give money gifts to each of their guests.
B. There is a big party with food, speeches and gifts.
C. The couple leave immediately for a honeymoon abroad.
D. Prayers are offered to the gods for a long marriage.
questions.explanation: Đáp án B. Sau lễ là tiệc chiêu đãi lớn: khách ăn uống, phát biểu, tặng tiền mừng. A, C, D không được nhắc.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 1

What is the writer’s main point in the last paragraph?
options: A. Shinto weddings are clearly better than Western ones.
B. Weddings in Japan are quickly becoming rare.
C. What the marriage means counts more than its style.
D. Money should never be given as a wedding gift.
questions.explanation: Đáp án C. Đoạn cuối chốt rằng ý nghĩa của lời hứa mới quan trọng, hơn là kiểu lễ. A đưa ra so sánh hơn-kém mà bài không khẳng định; B, D sai với nội dung.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

The word "smog" was formed by combining which two words?
options: A. "smoke" and "gas"
B. "smoke" and "fog"
C. "smoke" and "haze"
D. "mist" and "fog"
questions.explanation: Đáp án B. Bài nói rõ "smog" ghép từ "smoke" (khói) và "fog" (sương mù). Các phương án khác là bẫy âm gần giống.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

What happened during the Great Smog of London in 1952?
options: A. A huge fire burned down the city centre.
B. Heavy rain flooded the nearby coal mines.
C. Drivers crashed their cars in the thick fog.
D. Many people died after breathing the poisoned air.
questions.explanation: Đáp án D. Không khí độc khiến hàng nghìn người chết vì vấn đề hô hấp. A, B, C không được nhắc tới.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

Why did the smoke stay close to the ground for five days?
options: A. Cold weather and fog held it near the surface.
B. Nearby hills acted like walls around the city.
C. The heavy coal smoke was too dense to rise.
D. Falling snow dragged the smoke down to street level.
questions.explanation: Đáp án A. Thời tiết lạnh cùng sương mù giữ khói than sát mặt đất. B ngược với bài (không có gió mạnh); C, D không được nêu.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

How is photochemical smog created?
options: A. By hot sunlight drying out the thick winter fog.
B. By dirty air trapped between high mountains.
C. By sunlight acting on gases from vehicles.
D. By dust blown in from far-off deserts.
questions.explanation: Đáp án C. Loại smog này sinh ra khi ánh nắng phản ứng với khí thải xe hơi. A là smog than kiểu cũ; B, D không đúng.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

Why do cities surrounded by mountains suffer most from smog?
options: A. The mountains create extra smoke of their own.
B. The hills stop the polluted air from blowing away.
C. Steep mountain roads force cars to burn more fuel.
D. The mountains reflect extra sunlight onto the city.
questions.explanation: Đáp án B. Đồi núi như bức tường giữ không khí bẩn kẹt lại, không bị thổi đi. A, C, D đều không có căn cứ trong bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

According to the passage, why are the tiny particles in smog dangerous?
options: A. They can reach deep inside the lungs and the blood.
B. They cut visibility so badly that driving becomes dangerous.
C. They irritate the skin of children and elderly people.
D. They give healthy young adults asthma within days.
questions.explanation: Đáp án A. Hạt nhỏ đi sâu vào phổi, ngấm vào máu, tăng nguy cơ bệnh tim và hô hấp. B, C, D không phải điều bài nói về mối nguy sức khỏe.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

What may happen on the worst smog days?
options: A. Electricity is switched off across the city.
B. Nearby factories are closed down for the day.
C. People are paid by the city to stay home.
D. Schools shut and outdoor sports are called off.
questions.explanation: Đáp án D. Ngày tệ nhất, trường có thể đóng cửa và thể thao ngoài trời bị hủy, bệnh viện đông bệnh nhân. A, B, C không được nêu.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

Which solution to smog does the passage mention?
options: A. Forcing every citizen to wear a mask by law.
B. Building higher walls around every factory.
C. Restricting private cars to particular days of the week.
D. Charging drivers a fee to enter the city centre.
questions.explanation: Đáp án C. Một số thành phố cho xe cá nhân chạy chỉ vào ngày nhất định theo biển số. A, B, D không phải giải pháp được nêu.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

What does the example of London suggest?
options: A. Firm, steady action can slowly clean a city’s air.
B. Smog is something a city must simply endure.
C. Cold countries find it far easier to solve smog.
D. Planting trees is by far the single best answer.
questions.explanation: Đáp án A. London từng smog chết chóc nay không khí sạch hơn nhiều → hành động kiên quyết dần cải thiện được không khí. B, C, D trái với ý bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 2

Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a way cities fight smog?
options: A. Using electric buses in the city.
B. Letting private cars drive only on certain days.
C. Moving heavy industry away from homes.
D. Sharply raising the price of petrol.
questions.explanation: Đáp án D. Bài nêu xe buýt điện (A), vành đai cây xanh (B), dời công nghiệp nặng (C); nhưng KHÔNG nhắc việc tăng mạnh giá xăng.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What are "food trends"?
options: A. Strict rules about what everyone must eat.
B. The everyday dishes that ordinary families cook.
C. Popular dishes brought from Asia, Africa and Latin America.
D. Guesses about which foods will grow popular.
questions.explanation: Đáp án D. Đó là các dự đoán về món ăn/nguyên liệu/thói quen sẽ trở nên phổ biến. A, B, C hiểu sai khái niệm.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What is described as the biggest trend this year?
options: A. The growing love of spicy street food from abroad.
B. The growing popularity of food made from plants.
C. A strong new push to stop wasting food.
D. The spread of ordering meals through phone apps.
questions.explanation: Đáp án B. Xu hướng lớn nhất là thực phẩm từ thực vật lên ngôi. A trái nội dung; C, D không được nêu là lớn nhất.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

Besides health, why do some people choose plant-based meals?
options: A. Because good meat is getting harder to find.
B. Because vegetables tend to be the cheapest food.
C. Because producing meat needs much land and water.
D. Because raising animals is often seen as cruel.
questions.explanation: Đáp án C. Lý do khác là chăn nuôi tốn nhiều đất và nước. A, B, D không đúng với bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What does the passage suggest about plant-based "meat" products?
options: A. Their taste has improved a great deal over time.
B. They are still refused by most shoppers.
C. They cost far more than ordinary meat.
D. They are now proven to be healthier than real meat.
questions.explanation: Đáp án A. Bài cho thấy sản phẩm đã cải thiện nhiều về vị theo thời gian (từ lạ lẫm → giống thịt thật). B, C, D trái với ý bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

Why do many young people enjoy trying street food from other cultures?
options: A. Because it is served in luxury restaurants.
B. Because it is seen as healthier than eating at home.
C. Because the recipes are hard to find anywhere else.
D. Because it feels like travelling on a small budget.
questions.explanation: Đáp án D. Với người trẻ, đó là cách du lịch rẻ và thú vị mà không cần đi xa. A, B, C không đúng với bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What are some cooks now doing to reduce waste?
options: A. Using parts of food that were once thrown out.
B. Cooking much larger portions than before.
C. Refusing to serve any vegetables at all.
D. Freezing leftover food to keep it much longer.
questions.explanation: Đáp án A. Họ tận dụng những phần từng bị bỏ đi như vỏ rau, bánh mì cũ. B, C, D không đúng.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

How do the apps mentioned in the passage help?
options: A. They teach farmers how to grow more crops.
B. They let people buy leftover food at low prices.
C. They deliver hot meals to distant villages.
D. They check whether food is safe to eat.
questions.explanation: Đáp án B. Ứng dụng giúp khách mua đồ chưa bán hết với giá rẻ cuối ngày. A, C, D không được nêu.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What worry do critics have about technology and food?
options: A. That people forget how to cook without online videos.
B. That recipes found online are usually wrong.
C. That eating in front of a screen weakens real family meals.
D. That home fridges are becoming much too small.
questions.explanation: Đáp án C. Họ lo màn hình không thể thay cho việc cùng nhau nấu và ăn. A, B, D không phải nỗi lo được nêu.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What does the passage say about food trends in general?
options: A. Most new trends end up lasting for good.
B. Some fade fast while others become ordinary.
C. They stay much the same from year to year.
D. They are shaped mainly by a few famous chefs.
questions.explanation: Đáp án B. Một số xu hướng nhanh chóng biến mất, số ít thành thói quen thường ngày. A, C, D trái với bài.

questions.content:
reading — Passage 3

What is the writer’s main message in the final paragraph?
options: A. Our eating habits will go on evolving with what we value.
B. Most food trends vanish within just a few months.
C. Traditional cooking is better than all modern food.
D. Spending as little as possible is what matters most.
questions.explanation: Đáp án A. Đoạn cuối chốt thức ăn sẽ tiếp tục đổi thay theo mong muốn và giá trị của chúng ta. B, C, D không phản ánh thông điệp bài.
